Survey Solutions Listing Application

The Survey Solutions Listing Application forms an integral part of a comprehensive toolkit designed to enhance the process of survey implementation through Survey Solutions. This application provides valuable tools for enumerating and extracting survey units.

Key Features

  1. Enumeration of Buildings: Utilizing Enumeration Areas (e.g., those sampled with the JDC-Survey Solutions Spatial Sampling application), you can identify and enumerate all visible buildings within specified boundaries on Google Maps or Vantor (Maxar) satellite imagery via ‘vantorr’. The enumerated buildings form the second stage sampling frame, allowing for precise extraction of survey units within the cluster.

  2. Admin Interface: This intuitive interface lets you:

    • Extract all enumerated areas from the individual user directories of your collaborators.
    • Construct the frame, which becomes the basis for drawing the sample.

  3. Sample Drawing: For this stage, the application leverages the ‘spsurvey’ package, which facilitates the drawing of spatially balanced or random second-stage samples.

  4. Assignment to Supervisors: Once the sample is generated, you can assign it directly to the Survey Solutions supervisors. This assignment is performed through a streamlined interface grounded on ‘SurveySolutionsAPIv2’ (REST and GraphQL APIs).

Usage Overview

The Survey Solutions Listing Application not only accelerates survey implementation but also provides robust capabilities for managing complex survey projects. By enabling an efficient workflow from enumeration to sample extraction, this application stands as a vital resource for researchers and survey professionals.

For detailed information on how to get started, please consult our documentation.

Prerequisites

This application requires either a Google Maps API key (get yours here) when using provider = "google" (the default), or Vantor / Maxar API credentials when using provider = "vantor".

Installation

  1. Install R: https://cran.r-project.org/mirrors.html (version 4.1.1 or greater)

  2. Install RStudio: https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/

  3. Make sure the devtools package is installed, if not install it with:

install.packages("devtools")
  1. Install vantorr and susolisting from GitHub (CRAN dependencies including SurveySolutionsAPIv2 are installed automatically):
devtools::install_github("michael-cw/vantorr")
devtools::install_github("michael-cw/susolisting")

Running the application interactively

There are two options to run the application. The first one is in local mode, without admuser and admpass credentials provided. In this mode, the user needs to download their work with the enabled download button. The work is stored locally until the download button is clicked. Once the archive is created, the directory will be flushed, so make sure you have finished all the enumeration areas/segments and the downloaded file is safely stored.

library(susolisting)
# Default: Google Maps satellite imagery
susolisting::runListingApp()

# Or use Vantor / Maxar Vivid satellite imagery via leaflet + vantorr:
susolisting::runListingApp(provider = "vantor")

The second option allows you to run the application in team mode. This mode allows you to work with several desk enumerators either on the same device or everyone on their own devices, and copying the files to the administrator device. The administrator can then compile a single sampling frame based on all the enumerated areas, sample from it, and finally directly assign the sampled units to the survey teams on the Survey Solutions server. There is also a mapping module included, which allows you to map the frame variables to the Survey Solutions questionnaire Identification variables used on the Cover Page. The GPS location of the sample units is automatically assigned to the GPS variable from the identifying variables. To use this mode, run:

library(susolisting)
susolisting::runListingApp(admuser = "you", admpass = "your_password")

Running the application on a Shiny Server

The package also contains a Shiny Server function (open source or pro), which you can run, e.g., on an Ubuntu server or Virtual Machine. The same two modes are available. To run it on a Shiny Server, create a server directory (e.g., susolisting) and place an app.R script into this directory. If you run in local mode, the script contains the following two lines:

library(susolisting)
susolisting::runListingAppServer()

or in team mode:

library(susolisting)
susolisting::runListingAppServer(admuser = "you", admpass = "your_password")
